title: The Wire That Had 0.17 Ohm, Not 170
featured_title: THE WIRE THAT HAD 0.17 OHM NOT 170
subject: other-disciplines

presentation.challenge: The resistivity formula was correct, but 2 mm² was treated as 2×10^-9 m² instead of 2×10^-6 m². The wire resistance was 0.17 ohm.

practice.primary_question: How are material resistivity, conductor length, and cross-sectional area combined to calculate wire resistance?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Converting mm² to m² as if the linear millimeter conversion were not squared.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 2 mm² conductor area equals 2×10^-9 m².
case_dna.why_plausible: One millimeter is 10^-3 m, and the exponent is sometimes copied without squaring the length conversion.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: 2 mm²=2×10^-6 m². With rho=1.7×10^-8 ohm·m and L=20 m, R=rho L/A=0.17 ohm.
case_dna.corrected_model: Convert squared length units correctly, then use R=rho L/A.

problem_statement: A 20 m conductor has resistivity rho=1.7×10^-8 ohm·m and cross-sectional area 2.0 mm². A note converts the area to 2×10^-9 m² and reports 170 ohm. Determine the correct resistance, voltage drop at 10 A, and conductor power loss.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The resistance formula was right. The area conversion was not.

options.label: Use R=rho L/A with A=2×10^-6 m²
Use A=2×10^-9 m²
options.reason: That treats area like a linear unit.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The corrected area gives realistic electrical losses

cards.text: At 10 A, Vdrop=IR=1.7 V and P=I²R=17 W.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the conductor note
report: C3. Therefore A=2×10^-9 m² and R=170 ohm.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The squared-unit conversion is wrong by a factor of 1000.

evidence_choices.label: 2 mm²=2×10^-6 m² and R=0.17 ohm
evidence_choices.reason: This uses the correct squared conversion.

correction.template: R={resistance} ohm, Vdrop={voltage_drop} V, and P={power_loss} W.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply resistivity again
gates.prompt: For the same rho, L=10 m and A=1.0 mm². What is R?

options.label: 170 ohm
options.reason: That repeats the mm² conversion error.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the material-property calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that mm²-to-m² conversion must be squared before applying R=rho L/A.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The area unit was converted as a linear dimension.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Convert area correctly, then use R=rho L/A.

seo.seo_title: Electrical Resistivity and Wire Resistance | FE Other Disciplines E-099
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Other Disciplines E-099: a 20 m wire with rho 1.7×10^-8 ohm·m and 2 mm² area has 0.17 ohm resistance, not 170.
seo.excerpt: A squared-unit conversion error can change a conductor resistance by orders of magnitude.
seo.direct_answer: 2 mm²=2×10^-6 m². Therefore R=(1.7×10^-8)(20)/(2×10^-6)=0.17 ohm. At 10 A, voltage drop is 1.7 V and power loss is 17 W.
